According to The Globe & Mail's election predictor if the election was held today there is only a 1% chance that any party could claim a majority government, and I'm good with that. As a matter of fact the only way I will go to sleep with a smile on my face on election night is if no party gets to claim majority status.

In the interests of full disclosure I am hoping that it is an NDP minority that is formed, but I'll take an LPC minority. Heck, a CPC minority would even be interesting from an academic standpoint given that both Mulcair and Trudeau have publicly stated that they would not prop up a CPC minority, and unless they did the government would fall at the Speech From The Throne - can you imagine the national discussion that would take place when the GG, as I believe he would be bound to do so soon after an election, offered the Opposition party with the next greatest number of seats the opportunity to seek the confidence of The House?

But to get back to the reasons I want a minority government.

  1. I am weary beyond words over the arrogance that majority governments lead to. The leader of a majority government has virtual carte blanche to thumbs his or her nose at Parliament, the Senate, and the Canadian electorate for four long years. I want a Parliament where the party in power has to work with others in The House to pass legislation instead of simply issuing an edict ordering his/her caucus how they will vote on any particular issue. I want an end to debates and votes where the results are foregone conclusions before the legislation has even been introduced.

  2. I am weary beyond words over the power that party leaders have amassed over their caucus. I would love to see the party in power have such a slim number of caucus members that the departure of even one of them could potentially tip the balance of power. I want MPs to be elevated above their current status of "useful bench warmers for the party leader" (Stephen Harpers words, not mine), and a Parliament where MPs know they have that power.

  3. I am weary beyond words over the 'greatest minority' calling themselves a majority. 38 does not equal 54 and I want a Parliament that is representative of how we actually voted. There are only two parties with a reasonable chance of forming the next government who have promised to do that and I want them working together to make it happen.
I'm hoping for a minority government, what about you?
